clue.text: I should note friend with a perfect manner

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I should or I would
E is one of the musical notes of the scale
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to write a note to a friend in a model style.
explanation.walkthrough: I'D is the short form of 'I should'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a perfect manner is doing it as it would be done in an ideal world.

clue.text: Healthy accommodation for a prisoner charged with battery

definitions.text: Healthy accommodation for a prisoner charged with battery

parts.words: Healthy accommodation for a prisoner charged with battery
parts.note: a prison room free of damp would be healthy; charged and battery point to an electrical power source

explanation.surface: A decent prison room for someone accused of assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged with battery' suggests a criminal charge for assault, but it is electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical battery whose electrolyte is a paste rather than liquid, as in a torch battery.

parts.note: counting frames whose beads are moved by hand to calculate

explanation.surface: Computing machines that are worked manually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computers' means calculating devices, not electronic machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the bead counting frame, an ancient manual calculating device.

definitions.meaning: an old brand-like name for a friction match

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a fiendishly hard contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a contest but is the thing struck to make fire; the old friction match bore this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A name for Satan, and an old term for a match struck to light a fire.

indicators.note: messing about with something jumbles it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant afternoon spent pottering about in boats is what someone gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing about' rearranges the seven letters of IN BOATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to acquire or procure something is to get it.

parts.note: a secondary, little-used path off the main way

explanation.surface: A stroll someone seldom goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walk' is a path, not a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A side path or byway, one off the main route and so little used.

clue.text: It's released when one is agitated and in real trouble

definitions.text: It's released when one is agitated

indicators.note: being in trouble, the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something set loose when a person is stressed and genuinely in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in real trouble' looks like the end of the definition; 'trouble' rearranges AND IN REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone the body releases in response to fear, stress or excitement.

clue.text: The heart of the matter is that uncle is out to get us

indicators.note: out describes things put out of their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative is on the prowl for us, and that is the core issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges UNCLE, then US is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The central core of an atom or cell, hence the heart of matter itself.

definitions.meaning: grasping or comprehending, as in getting a joke

explanation.surface: Someone is becoming kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is not becoming, but comprehending.
explanation.definitionFit: Comprehension, as in getting it, and sympathetic, as in an understanding friend.

clue.text: Bird able to speak, surprising many

indicators.note: taken as surprising or startling the letters, which are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A talking bird astonishes a great number of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' rearranges MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: This starling relative of Asia is famous for mimicking human speech.

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn, so cons means studies
seizing a ship or aircraft by force is piracy

explanation.surface: Someone researches a scheme to seize an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is a crossword favourite for study, as in conning one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret scheme among several people, a plot, is a synonym.

parts.note: to belie something is to show it to be false, contradicting it
f, for forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A view is being shouted down by an objector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' is not a homophone signal here: it gives F, the music abbreviation for forte.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a conviction one holds is a view or opinion.

clue.text: No longer minded being drawn out?

parts.note: ex- describes something that is former, no longer so
to mind a child or a shop is to tend it

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped caring is having the truth pulled out of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minded' means looked after, not objected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lengthened or prolonged has been drawn out.

clue.text: A hole in one, perhaps, for mariner's dependant

definitions.meaning: in golf a score of three under par on a hole, achieved by an ace on a par four
the seabird hung around the neck of Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, so it depended from him

explanation.surface: A sailor's family member makes a golfing ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dependant' puns on something hanging down; the bird was hung from the Mariner's neck as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a golf score three below par, and the great seabird of Coleridge's poem.

parts.note: an act is a law, and repealing it brings about its end

explanation.surface: The final moment of a stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' suggests theatre but means a statute; doing away with it is its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal doing away with a law or institution, which ends it.

clue.text: Stop up for the end of play

definitions.meaning: to shut or seal an opening
in cricket, the finish of a day's play is called this

explanation.surface: Someone asks to block a gap so that the game can finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Close of play is the end of a cricket day, a phrase also used loosely in British offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting a hole is one sense; the finish or conclusion is another, pronounced differently.

clue.text: In short, a form of school punishment

definitions.text: In short, a form of school punishment

parts.words: In short, a form of school punishment
parts.note: an imposition, lines set as a punishment in British schools, is abbreviated in school slang

explanation.surface: A brief description of a schoolroom penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' says the word is a clipped form of imposition, extra written work set as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British school slang for a written penalty such as lines, shortened from imposition.

clue.text: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?

definitions.text: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?

parts.words: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?
parts.note: the proverb says to do this while the sun shines; literally, farmers dried grass in the open

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathed shamelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'make hay while the sun shines' means seize your chance; literally it is drying cut grass in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for exploiting a favourable moment, literally drying cut grass in sunny fields.

clue.text: It's not acceptable to make money on a game

parts.note: something bad is not acceptable
to mint is to make coins

explanation.surface: Profiting from gambling on sport is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make money' means literally striking coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a net, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Inadequate man produces a lower output at work

definitions.text: Inadequate man produces a lower output at work

parts.words: Inadequate man produces a lower output at work
parts.note: a lower is a cow that lows, its output is milk, and at work suggests op, an opus

explanation.surface: A weak employee gets less done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not less, but a mooing cow, whose product, milk, starts the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, timid man lacking courage, an old term of contempt.

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist that rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: Eggs being converted into joyful shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges INTO to give TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonged applause and cheering from an audience is a synonym.

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
someone who has aged has grown visibly older

explanation.surface: Someone gained weight and grew older-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on weight' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Put on' is the definition, as a play is put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A production that has been mounted or presented has been put on.

definitions.meaning: allowed in, as a patient taken into hospital

explanation.surface: Something presumed without question.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'taken for granted' splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is let in or received; the other is conceded or confessed.

clue.text: Such a cleaning brush will be barely used

definitions.text: Such a cleaning brush will be barely used

parts.words: Such a cleaning brush will be barely used
parts.note: a bath sponge made from a dried gourd is used on the naked body, so barely is literal

explanation.surface: A scrubbing brush that hardly ever gets used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean hardly ever, but it means on bare skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough fibrous bath scrubber made from a dried gourd, used when washing naked.

parts.note: the word names both a large pipe instrument and a periodical that voices a group's views

explanation.surface: A magazine about music.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a keyboard instrument and a publication, such as a party organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe keyboard instrument, and a newspaper or periodical speaking for a group.

clue.text: Their members were bound to work under strict supervision

definitions.text: Their members were bound to work under strict supervision

parts.words: Their members were bound to work under strict supervision
parts.note: groups of convicts were literally chained together while labouring under guard

explanation.surface: A workforce obliged to labour under close watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' seems to mean obliged, but the convicts were physically shackled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of prisoners shackled together and made to do outdoor labour under guards.

parts.note: read as the way a pedestrian walks rather than a path for walkers

explanation.surface: A footpath for people on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkway' is split into walk and way: a manner of walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's manner of walking or stride is this word.

indicators.note: alarming the letters throws them into disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worrying rot has set in within a poisonous material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarming' rearranges DECAY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly poison, so an example of a toxic substance.

parts.note: a door is a gap one passes through, and a chance is also called this

explanation.surface: A door that leads to a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a physical aperture like a door and a chance or vacancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or aperture, and also a chance or vacancy, hence an opportunity.
